answer: One concrete defense is proof of useful work tied to a scarce resource: before an agent can join, it must produce a costly, checkable signal, such as solving a puzzle whose difficulty rises with the number of identities from the same source. Creating ten thousand fake agents then costs ten thousand times the work of one. Like layers of shale that only form under sustained pressure, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be faked overnight. A raven appearing from nowhere with no history is treated as untrusted until it has done the work, so large-scale sybil farming becomes uneconomic.
